label: TP
reason: Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) is a true positive: user input flows from request.getParameter() through param/bar/doSomething() into the sql variable at line 56, which is then used in JDBC template queries (queryForLong/queryForObject). This constitutes SQL injection. Alert 1 (java/xss) is a false positive: while the sql string contains user input, it is only rendered to the response writer in the catch block where it is explicitly encoded via ESAPI.encodeForHTML(), preventing XSS.

evidence.note: User input flows into sql variable via bar/doSomething(); sql is used in DatabaseHelper queries (SQL injection risk). In catch block, sql is encoded before output.
Concatenation creates sql string; however, actual output goes through encodeForHTML() in catch block, mitigating XSS
